page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7t.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server built on x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz, it provides 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading running two threads per core. The processor includes 48 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and instruction set support for AVX-512, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI extensions. System memory totals 48.0 GB, establishing a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB allocated per vCPU core. The server includes no bundled local SSD storage and features an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth capability without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance evaluation across benchmark suites places the instance primarily within average middle-tier performance brackets. In stress-ng testing, the server recorded a single-core score of 1881.48 and a multi-core score of 11646.62. Uncached memory bandwidth tests registered 78.98 GB/sec for large reads and 52.5 GB/sec for large writes. Application benchmarks demonstrate baseline competence for standard execution tasks, achieving 12.02 million operations per second in Redis SET execution, 17.22 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7934.0. The primary performance tradeoff appears in machine learning workloads; without accelerator hardware, prompt processing for a 7B parameter model yields 24.27 tokens per second, falling into the bottom quartile of benchmark outputs.

The qualitative resource efficiency of ecs.g7t.3xlarge derives from its balanced provision of CPU compute, memory capacity, and standard 8 Gbps network access without the cost overhead of dedicated GPUs or specialized local storage arrays. Workloads that depend on network-attached storage and standard multi-threaded CPU execution match this hardware profile. Appropriate deployment targets include web serving, microservice hosting, software compilation, medium-scale database operations, and memory-cached application backends.
